extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and journalists (reporters covering international conferences)
extracted.subtask_description: Coverage and procedural reporting of the United Nations (United Nations Food) Conference at Hot Springs, Va., including the conference's proposed objectives, recommended outputs, and press-access arrangements. Also covers related wartime items (OWI pamphlet controversy, Army investigations) as reported to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of nutrition
rubrics_metrics.description: The newly recognized importance of nutrition as fundamental to well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first of seven tentative objectives the U.S. delegation suggests the conference prepare/approve and report on; intended as a foundation for discussion among the 44 delegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of establishing action in support of nutritional goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility of establishing action, suitably representing all United Nations and associated nations, in support of agreed nutritional goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. delegates put this second in the seven-point tentative schedule as a practical follow-up step—emphasis on creating actionable measures and international representation/co-ordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of agriculture in meeting basic human needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of agriculture in meeting basic human needs in a way that contributes to progress and order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the tentative objectives: reports should stress agriculture's central role in fulfilling nutritional goals and in postwar stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for changes in agriculture to meet modern world needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of changes in agriculture to facilitate more effective fulfillment of the needs of the modern world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. delegates propose that the conference identify and recommend agricultural changes necessary for improved global nutrition and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of stepping up production of lacking items
rubrics_metrics.description: The possibility of stepping up greatly the production of things now lacked by tens of millions of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at identifying realistic opportunities to increase production postwar; presented as a core objective to be examined in conference reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution of food steps to an expanding world economy
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of these steps (nutrition/agricultural/production measures) as a contribution toward achieving a constantly expanding world economy in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame nutritional/production recommendations in the larger economic context—show how measures support world economic expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies to expand exchange of goods and consumption capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of policies making for a larger and wider exchange of goods and the increasing of consumption capacity simultaneously with the world's capacity to produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference reports should address trade and policy measures that increase consumption capability in step with production increases, to ensure equitable distribution and demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference should issue a brief, ringing declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference should issue a declaration in brief and ringing terms to make the conclusions embodied in the report more widely known and understood by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. delegates incline to this view to give the report new clarity and public visibility beyond technical reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and approve reports on specified food/nutrition topics
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclave should prepare, approve and issue certain reports dealing with the listed objectives (nutrition, agriculture, production, policies, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports are intended to provide a basis for discussion among delegations and may resemble prior special-group reports but will carry the authority of an intergovernmental assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a continuing commission for follow-up and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of a continuing commission charged with the duty of reporting on the functions and the execution of declarations and recommendations of the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission would have ongoing authority to monitor coordination and expansion of international organizational efforts in the field of food and to follow up on conference recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend governments pledge appropriate national action
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference should recommend to member governments that they pledge to their peoples and to each other that after the war they will assume a new and continuing responsibility for seeing that their peoples are better fed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommendation aimed at encouraging national commitments and implementation of conference conclusions via appropriate domestic policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press access arrangements at the conference (restricted hotel access / pressroom interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsmen are restricted from entering the conference hotel; delegates are reachable by telephone and may step down to an on-grounds pressroom for interviews; chairmen will hold press conferences at stated times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters argue these arrangements prevent spontaneous conversations, reduce opportunities for questioning delegates, and limit the scope of information available; the chairman says scheduled briefings will keep reporters abreast of action and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance public access with confidentiality (ACLU protest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Precautions taken to restrict press activities at the conference should be relaxed insofar as consistent with protection of confidential discussion, so as not to deprive the public of rightful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The American Civil Liberties Union wired the Secretary of State protesting that arrangements were more stringent than warranted and urged relaxation while acknowledging need for secrecy in executive sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OWI materials should present a balanced, fair discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of War Information's discussion guide on 1943 tax problems (including 'pay-as-you-go') should give a balanced and fair presentation of all sides, outlining advantages and disadvantages and discussing alternatives without urging political action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OWI Director Elmer Davis defended the pamphlet as 'balanced'—it starts by outlining advantages of the skip-a-year plan, includes fair statements both for and against the Ruml plan, and does not tell readers to write letters to influence Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold public reference while remedial action is taken (investigations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A committee may make no prior public reference to an ongoing matter in order to give the responsible agency an opportunity to take corrective steps to assure any defective parts in use are repaired or replaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserting that investigations are continuing and final reports must await completion of all studies; committee holding private hearings with possibility of public hearings later.
